And when he went out, he stood at the head of the square and said:
"O people of Aleppo!
I was brought up by you and placed in your care,
and I have no father or brother besides you."
And as he said these things, he was nearly choked with weeping.
And all the people wept, and they lifted up their voices with wailing, and said:
"We are all your servants, and we will die before you."
The Franks also sent messengers to Saladin and censured him:
"This thing is not done [properly],
that you render evil for good to the son of (to the house of) your lord.
And if you do not listen to us and turn away from Aleppo,
behold, we will all come against you."
When Saladin saw that the affair was not proceeding according to his wish,
and that it was not possible to persuade the people of Aleppo,
he turned back and went to Baalbek and took it.
And he came from there to Homs,
and he also took its citadel.
Now the people of Aleppo sent to Sayf al-Din, the lord of Mosul, and said to him:
"If you are negligent and let Saladin take Aleppo,
do not think that Mosul will remain yours."
Sayf al-Din immediately sent a large force with his brother 'Izz al-Din Mas'ud,
and they came to Aleppo.
And they and the people of Aleppo assembled, and they went and encamped against Hama,
and they sent an envoy to Saladin at Homs.
And they demanded of him that he restore all the fortresses he had taken to the son of his lord,
and that Damascus alone should remain his,
yet that he should be in it as one of the emirs, in subjection to al-Malik al-Salih.
Saladin, however, replied:
"I have not come to make war with the son of my lord,
but to protect him and guard his lands and his treasuries,
and from what you say I will not depart at all."
And when they saw that he inclined toward peace,
they thought that he was weak,
and they treated him with contempt.
And they said:
"You shall not remain in Syria at all,
but you shall enter Egypt,
and there is nothing for you from us except the sword."
And they marched out and encamped against al-Rastan,
and Saladin also came to meet them.
And they met each other at a place called the Horns of Hama,
and the people of Mosul and the people of Aleppo were defeated,
and they turned their backs to flee.
And Saladin restrained his forces
from pursuing the fugitives too far,
and from killing anyone.
